observations: Single photo shows a bare automotive engine assembly, removed from a vehicle, resting on a concrete floor.
Visible parts: radiator, drive belt and pulleys, valve cover, oil filler cap, some wiring and hoses.
Surface shows dust, grime, and some surface corrosion on metal brackets and bolts.
No engine code, VIN, or manufacturer stamp is legible anywhere in the image.
Watermark reads 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'BARRY BEST GENERAL', a seller/platform stamp, not proof of the item's identity.
No power test, compression test, or running video is shown.

identity.kind: used car engine (seller claims Acura RDX, 2008-2010)

claims.evidence: No import documentation, customs sticker, or shipping tag visible in photo 0.
No engine code, casting number, or VIN tag is readable in photo 0; shape alone cannot confirm make/model/year range.

risks.risk: Engine may not be the claimed Acura RDX model/displacement, or may be a mismatched or rebadged unit.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting stamp or VIN-linked tag, clearly legible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unverified used engine, not specifically as Acura RDX

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (compression, bearings, timing issues) not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Video of the engine running/idling with audio, plus a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Unknown mileage and service history, common with tokunbo engines.
risks.proof: Photo of odometer from source vehicle or any accompanying paperwork tying mileage to this unit.

risks.risk: Visible corrosion and grime may hide leaks, cracked housings, or missing components not seen from this single angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from all sides (front, rear, underside) and close-ups of oil pan, head gasket area, and connectors.

risks.risk: Completeness of accessories (sensors, manifolds, starter, alternator) cannot be confirmed from one partial photo.
risks.proof: Full-engine photos showing all sides with accessories attached or an itemized list with photos.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code or casting number stamped on the block.
Video of the engine running with sound.
Photos from additional angles: rear, underside, and both sides of the engine.
Any documentation (shipping/customs papers) supporting the 'tokunbo' claim.
response.reason: The item is clearly a used automotive engine, but the claimed brand, model, and year cannot be confirmed from the photo, and no functional test is shown, so it must be priced as a generic unverified used engine in worst-case (unknown-running) condition.
